families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer-rich films use retained acid and plasticised polar domains to preserve proton pathways across the cold-to-room window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES/plasticised polar domains are supported in chitosan blends and are preferred for low-temperature continuity.
D3: biopolymer/PVA-type hosts are analogously flexible and hydrogen-bonded rather than brittle when plasticised.
D4: phosphoric-acid or DES acid speciation is supported as a confined non-crystallising proton source.
D6: starch, chitosan, and PVA provide dense donor/acceptor networks for proton relay.
D7: chitosan and low-loaded phosphoric-acid systems show conducting-phase retention emphasis.

families.family_description: One-dimensional clay hosts confine and retain hydrated acid within guided nanoscale channels that can stay connected at low temperature.
descriptor_match: D2: bound acid/water continuity is plausible in clay-confined polar domains under cold operation.
D4: phosphoric acid in confinement or DES-like acid complexes supports non-crystallising proton-source behavior.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite directly support interconnected nanoconfinement/channel guidance.
D7: fibrous/tubular clays are reported to improve acid retention and reduce leaching.

families.family_description: Amorphous phosphate-rich networks provide continuous proton pathways and dense hydrogen-bond functionality with strong phase retention.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is directly reported as an amorphous continuous transport medium.
D4: phosphate-rich acidic environments analogously stabilize proton-carrying species without crystallisation.
D6: phosphate networks and phosphoric acid supply dense relay-capable donor/acceptor sites.
D7: phosphate matrices strongly retain the conducting phase, though some reports note stability caveats.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane combining chitosan as the biopolymer host, PVA as the film-forming plasticisable phase, attapulgite as a 1-D confinement filler, and phosphoric acid as the proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity via hydrogen-bonded chitosan/PVA domains
nanoconfinement: 1-D attapulgite may guide connected acid channels
retention: clay-plus-biopolymer host should reduce acid loss versus free PA
risk_flags: PA leaching remains possible at high acid loading
subzero flexibility is inferred rather than directly demonstrated

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is reported as an acid-interacting scaffold with confinement/retention behavior and tolerates high water uptake without disintegration.
PVA contributes OH-rich hydrogen-bonding functionality and serves as an analogous flexible film-forming partner.
Attapulgite is directly reported to provide 1-D channel guidance, nanoconfinement, and acid immobilisation.
Phosphoric acid is supported as a mobile proton source in complexed environments and as the hydrogen-bonded conducting medium.

instances.novelty_rationale: This combines the requested quaternary synergy elements into one cold-oriented membrane concept. The exact four-part combination is not directly present in the evidence pool, but each role is individually supported by close analogs.

instances.composition_description: A starch–PVA blend plasticised by an in-situ choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep eutectic to create a retained acid-rich conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES-like plasticisation should suppress freezing/disruptive crystallisation
proton_relay: starch/PVA OH groups plus PA support hybrid proton transfer
film_integrity: blended polysaccharide/synthetic host may retain the polar phase better than neat acid
risk_flags: DES-water balance may drift during humidification cycling
acid overloading could soften the film excessively

element_evidence.reason: Starch is supported as an OH-rich channel-forming and proton-relay component.
PVA provides complementary OH-mediated hydrogen bonding and film formation.
Choline chloride is directly linked to phosphoric-acid deep-eutectic formation that can stabilize the acid form.
Phosphoric acid supplies the proton-conducting phase and participates in DES-like non-crystallising acid speciation.

instances.novelty_rationale: The novelty is the simultaneous use of a starch/PVA host with a ChCl/PA eutectic-style proton phase for subambient operation. Evidence supports the host H-bond network and the acid-complexing motif separately, but not this exact integrated formulation.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan matrix loaded with phosphoric-acid-filled halloysite nanotubes to confine and retain the conducting acid inside tubular nanospace.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: PA@HNT-style tubular hosting should maintain connected proton domains
retention: HNT–acid interactions may lower phosphoric-acid leaching
cold_window: confined acid in a hydrated biopolymer host is plausible for subzero continuity
risk_flags: interfacial aggregation of HNTs could interrupt pathways
direct low-temperature conductivity evidence is not available for this exact mix

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is an acid-retaining scaffold and a suitable analog host for confined proton phases.
HNTs are directly reported to host phosphoric acid in nanotubular confinement and reduce leaching.
Phosphoric acid is the supported proton source and conducting hydrogen-bonded fluid in confined composite membranes.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is a cross-paper combination marrying chitosan retention behavior with PA@HNT confinement. The evidence strongly supports each component role, but the exact ternary formulation is not explicitly reported in the pool.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane containing phosphotungstic acid immobilised on 1-D attapulgite filler to form guided nanoscale proton channels.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: attapulgite-guided channels are directly supported
proton_relay: PWA adds dense acidic relay sites within the scaffold
retention: chitosan plus attapulgite are reported to immobilise the acid phase
risk_flags: high-temperature evidence dominates the source report
heteropolyacid hydration dependence may complicate deep-cold use

element_evidence.reason: This paper directly describes chitosan as the percolated acid-interacting scaffold in the composite.
PWA is directly reported as the proton-relay acid immobilised within the membrane.
Attapulgite is directly reported as the 1-D host enabling confinement and acid retention.

instances.novelty_rationale: This exact reported composite is retained as a control because it directly demonstrates the clay-confined acid-scaffold design logic. It anchors the candidate set with one literature-near benchmark.

instances.instance_name: Phosphate glass/phosphoric acid/carbon dot hybrid membrane
instances.composition_description: An amorphous phosphate-rich matrix is modified with phosphoric acid and carbon dots to combine intrinsic protonic continuity with nanoscale pathway organisation.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous phosphate network should avoid crystallisation-driven interruptions
proton_relay: phosphate groups plus PA provide dense donor/acceptor functionality
nanostructure: carbon dots may improve dispersed ordering of conducting domains
risk_flags: glass-process compatibility with added PA/CDs may be difficult
long-term retention can be conditional in phosphate systems

element_evidence.reason: Phosphate glass is directly supported as an amorphous proton-conducting matrix with dense hydrogen bonding and strong, though conditionally stable, retention.
Phosphoric acid provides the proton source and hydrogen-bonded conducting medium in analogous composites.
Carbon dots are reported to create a more ordered dispersed structure consistent with improved interconnected confinement.

instances.novelty_rationale: This concept fuses an amorphous phosphate transport matrix with PA and nanoscale ordering additives for cold-resilient continuity. The combination is novel relative to the pool, which supports the matrix and additive roles separately.
